### Observed differences

- In the later window, four activities that were absent throughout the earlier window — A32, A33, A38 and A39 — each occur in about 47 in 100 traces (94–96 of 200), at mid-trace positions (median relative position about 0.5). [OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- These four behave as a connected block: A26 now leads into them in about 47 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before, about 96 in 100 went to A27); transitions stay largely within the block or exit to A28 (from A32: about 32 in 100 to A28, 30 to A33, 21 to A39, 16 to A38); block members co-occur in about 47 in 100 traces; and they almost never co-occur with A27 (at most about 1 in 100 traces). [DIR007, DIR009, REL028, REL034, REL038]
- A27, previously present in every trace, now runs in about 54 in 100; the share of traces where A27 precedes A28, A47 or A48 fell from essentially all cases to about 53 in 100. [OCC006, REL027, REL032, REL033]
- A04 drops from about 65 in 100 traces to about 17 in 100 and, when present, sits much earlier (median relative position about 0.96 vs 0.47); its dominant edge to A48 (about 90 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) weakens to about 19 in 100, while A47's edge to A04 (about 64 in 100 of A47's transitions) nearly disappears (about 3 in 100) in favour of A47→A48 (about 35 → 85 in 100), which now typically follows A47 immediately (85 in 100 at distance 1, vs 35 before). [OCC002, POS001, DIR002, DIR013, LAG005, REL011]
- A14 and A15, present in all traces throughout, are now followed by the new block in about 47 in 100 traces (they never co-occurred with A32/A33/A38/A39 before), and the A26→A28 distance stretches from mostly 2 steps to a split between 2 and 5 steps. [REL013, REL018, LAG002]
- Participation rises modestly for A02 (about 5 → 17 in 100), A06 (3 → 20), A08 (7 → 16) and A10 (7 → 18), with their outgoing transitions spreading over many more targets. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004]
- A few lag-based items rest on very few later observations (A47→A04: 8; A04→A48: 11) and are weakly supported. [LAG004, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, roughly half of the executions take an alternative mid-process route: after A14, A15 or A26, the flow passes through the newly observed block A32–A33–A38–A39 and continues into A28 and A47/A48, running in place of the previously universal A27, whose participation fell from all traces to about 54 in 100 and which almost never appears together with the block. A second, related shift is that the earlier A47→A04→A48 routing is largely replaced by a direct A47→A48 handover, leaving A04 rare (about 17 in 100 traces) and early-positioned. [OCC006, OCC007, DIR007, DIR009, DIR013, REL013, REL028, REL034, REL041, LAG005]

This judgement rests on direct relational and positional evidence — the block sits at mid-trace positions, is preceded by A14/A15/A26 and precedes A28/A47/A48 in the order relations, and the successor profiles of A26, A04 and A47 shifted accordingly — and on volume: 86 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected by chance in an unchanged process, so the pattern as a whole is unlikely to be a screening artefact. [POS003, DIR007, DIR009, REL023, REL041, DIR013]

Limitations: the two windows are finite samples, so variant frequencies can differ between them without any change and a rare variant can appear in one window only; the block's appearance in about 95 of 200 later traces after 200 earlier traces without it makes pure sampling noise implausible but cannot exclude a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants. Many items describe the same underlying traces (the block's relations with A14, A15 and A26 are near-identical) and are therefore not independent confirmations, and zero participation in the earlier window means only that A32/A33/A38/A39 were not observed there. [OCC007, REL013, REL018, REL023]
